title: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd - 500570 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: India PV margins squeezed by commodities with only ~40% offset via price and cost; JLR FY27 EBIT guidance cut to 2-3% and cash outflow to ~£1.25bn, while India volumes remain strong.

summary.headline: Tata Motors PV Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue ~₹96,000–97,000 crore (+34% YoY) with EBIT margin 1.1%; JLR cut FY27 EBIT guidance to 2–3%.
summary.overview: Consolidated TMPV revenue rose about 34% YoY to roughly ₹96,000–97,000 crore, with EBITDA margin 6.2% and EBIT margin 1.1%, down from 2.4% in Q1 on adverse JLR mix and commodity pressure in India. Exceptional charges of ₹6,700 crore were booked in the quarter for JLR restructuring. Domestic volumes hit a record 67,000 units a month average with 14.3% Vahan share, while EVs reached a record ~16,000 units a month with 43% share. JLR sold 82,000 units at £5.9 billion revenue, flat QoQ, but PBT fell to £6 million on China and MENA weakness and mix; FY27 JLR guidance was lowered.

financial_highlights.change: expected to close FY27 near ₹47,000 crore

financial_highlights.metric: JLR H1 cash outflow (incl. working capital)

segments.name: India PV (TMPV domestic)
segments.commentary: Q2 volumes were a record ~67,000 units/month average (+40% YoY), 14.3% Vahan share; October 2026 record 75,000 units at 14.8% share. EVs ~16,000 units/month (nearly 2x YoY) at 43% share; EV penetration 23%, CNG penetration ~25% of industry.

segments.name: JLR
segments.commentary: Q2 wholesale 82,000 units, revenue £5.9 billion, EBIT 2% H1, Q2 PBT £6 million. China wholesale down 45% YoY in the quarter and 36% YTD; MENA also weak. Defender up over 20% YoY; Range Rover and Defender up QoQ, Discovery mix higher.

guidance_outlook: JLR FY27 guidance revised: EBIT margin 2–3% (below prior guidance) and cash outflow of about £1.25 billion.
JLR targets double-digit EBITDA margin and positive cash generation in FY28, and return to net cash by end FY30.
JLR targets 10% annual top-line growth and resetting break-even volume to 300,000 units; £1.7 billion cost savings committed over two years.
India: domestic capex 6–7% of revenue in FY27 (no absolute number given); H1 capex ~₹2,700 crore, expected to run higher over the next 18–24 months.

India: additional price increase considered in Q3 and a further, slightly higher one in Q4 FY27; YTD price hikes ~1.7% across April, July and September; calibrated pricing and cost actions offset ~40% of commodity increase YTD.
Industry H2 growth expected to moderate due to high base post-GST; commodity pressure to stay adverse in Q3; commodity curve expected to flatten in Q4.
capex_capacity: JLR H1 investment ₹1.76 billion (£1.76 billion); H2 expected marginally below H1, then declining into FY28; £11.5 billion of a £15–18 billion five-year programme already invested.
JLR five new vehicles launching over next 18 months including Range Rover BEV, Range Rover Sport BEV, Jaguar Type 01; Range Rover GT to launch as BEV early next year.
India EV production being raised from ~16,000 to ~20,000 units/month within 2–3 months; Sierra capacity being scaled; Ares capacity being expanded from ~4,000 units/month plan.
India PLI: about 40% of eligible models covered; two pending models have A18 but await final approval; cumulative approvals ~₹831 crore in H1 (Q2 ~₹531 crore).
demand_pricing: Industry PV volumes 1.36 million in Q2 (+29% YoY); EVs industry volume +70% YoY; CNG+EV combined about one-third of industry volume.
India EV bookings ~30% of total bookings; EVs are 40–45% of pending bookings; EV inventory ~10 days vs ~27–28 days overall (including 6–7 days transit).
Sierra sold over 70,000 units this year; Ares sold over 4,000 units in its first month, limited by production; Punch EV first EV to cross 5,000 units in a month.
JLR: Range Rover BEV has ~5,000 orders before public drive; China market down ~30% and JLR China share used to be ~70% of its portfolio (pre-this year); CHERY-related IP protection being pursued.
JLR residual value pressure in lower-end portfolio from competitive pricing in UK; Chinese OEM exports up ~4 million units YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What share of bookings are EVs, and what are waiting periods?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 30% of bookings are EVs, and 40–45% of pending bookings are EVs; EV inventory is about 10 days versus 27–28 days overall, with production rising from ~16,000 to ~20,000 a month in 2–3 months.

qa_highlights.question: Commodity outlook for Q3 and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity pressure persists in Q3 (copper especially); management expects a price increase in Q3 possibly and a higher one in Q4, taken gradually to avoid demand shock.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic capex for FY27 and PLI roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic capex guided at 6–7% of revenue for FY27; about 40% of models are PLI-covered, with two more awaiting final approval and minimum run rate of ~₹500+ crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did JLR cut guidance and what is the China plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the cut to China and mix; China plans to be updated next quarter, with JLR staying invested and watching the market closely.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving JLR cash turnaround and investment decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment peak from five launches (£11.5 billion spent of £15–18 billion programme) will decline over 18–24 months; EBITDA to rise as new vehicles launch.

qa_highlights.question: Cost savings and voluntary redundancy?
qa_highlights.answer: About 4,000 headcount reduction with ~3,000 leaving this FY; ~£400 million per year of ongoing savings, not all in P&L as some engineering roles are capitalised; £530 million restructuring charge in Q2 (£295 million VRS).

risks_watch: JLR China volume decline and possible further guidance changes; China plan due next quarter.
Commodity inflation (copper, aluminium, steel, rubber, petrochemicals) and FX resets pressuring India margins; PLI expiry in 2028.
JLR break-even volume of 300,000 units versus 82,000 quarterly sales; residual value pressure in UK.
EV supply chain: semiconductor and DRAM constraints being monitored; cell supply from a partner with sister company Agratas to begin production.
Industry growth rates expected to moderate in H2 after high base.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India demand and product momentum, but cautious on margins and explicit that JLR guidance is being cut due to China, mix and the cost reset. Management was evasive on China specifics and deferred detail to the next quarter.
key_quotes: So we will have to change our FY 27 guidance, now expecting EBIT under 2 to 3% range and cash outflow of circa 1.25 billion pounds.
We delivered our highest level quarterly volume support to lack units, representing 40% year on year growth.
So the big story is the mixed deterioration by brand and by country.

adds.what: India EV production raised from ~16,000 to ~20,000 units/month
Ares capacity expansion from ~4,000 units/month plan
JLR five new vehicles over next 18 months incl. Range Rover BEV, Range Rover Sport BEV, Jaguar Type 01

growth.why: JLR cut FY27 EBIT guidance to 2-3% with a £1.25bn cash outflow, while the 10% p.a. top-line aim is held and India volumes are at records (67k/month, +40% YoY) with EV capacity rising from ~16k to ~20k/month within 2-3 months, though most growth targets are medium-term and the FY27 outlook is mixed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: FY28 for JLR; Q4 FY27 for India
rows.why: JLR targets double-digit EBITDA/EBIT in FY28 with £1.7bn cost savings over two years, while India pricing (~1.7% YTD plus further hikes in Q3 and Q4) offset only ~40% of commodity inflation and the Q2 EBIT margin fell to 1.1% from 2.4%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: India EV production being raised from ~16,000 to ~20,000 units/month within 2-3 months, with Ares capacity expansion and Sierra scaling under way, and JLR's five new vehicles launching over the next 18 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: India domestic volumes hit a record ~67,000 units/month in Q2 (+40% YoY) with EV supply rising from ~16,000 to ~20,000/month and EV inventory at ~10 days, though industry H2 growth is expected to moderate after the high base.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: India domestic capex guided at 6-7% of revenue for FY27 with H1 capex of ~₹2,700 crore expected to run higher over the next 18-24 months, and JLR's £11.5bn of a £15-18bn five-year programme already spent.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: JLR H1 EBIT margin is only 2% and Q2 PBT fell to £6 million, while commodity pressure stays adverse in Q3 and industry H2 growth is expected to moderate after the high post-GST base.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: JLR already cut FY27 EBIT guidance to 2-3% and the China plan is due next quarter, while China wholesale fell 45% YoY in Q2 and 36% YTD, leaving further risk to JLR numbers.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: next 18 months (Range Rover BEV, Range Rover Sport BEV, Jaguar Type 01 in Q2 window onwards)
rows.why: JLR has five new vehicles launching over the next 18 months, including Range Rover BEV with ~5,000 orders before public drive, and Range Rover GT moves to BEV early next year.

rows.label: Further India price hikes in Q3 and Q4 FY27
rows.why: Management considers an additional price increase in Q3 and a slightly higher one in Q4, after ~1.7% YTD hikes, to offset commodity inflation of which only ~40% has been covered so far.

rows.label: JLR net cash by end FY30; net debt near ₹47,000 crore at FY27 close
rows.when: FY27 close; FY30 for JLR net cash
rows.why: Consolidated net debt of ₹51,000 crore is expected to fall to about ₹47,000 crore by FY27 close, and JLR aims for positive cash generation in FY28 and net cash by end FY30.

rows.label: JLR £1.7bn cost savings and ~4,000 headcount reduction
rows.when: over two years; ~3,000 leaving this FY
rows.why: JLR has committed £1.7bn of savings over two years, with ~£400m per year of ongoing savings and a £530m Q2 restructuring charge including £295m VRS.

tone.note: Management was confident on India demand, record volumes and EV ramp, but cautious on margins and JLR, and evasive on China detail, deferring it to next quarter; analysts pressed on the JLR guidance cut and China exposure.
